scope: Primary-source review of hardware stop and failed runtime suspend, not hardware qualification

primary_upstream_reset.reason: NGD remote instance and remotely controlled BAM lose state during power cycling; suspend/resume DMA reinitialization prevents stale setup and transaction timeouts
primary_upstream_reset.contract: This explains DMA reset necessity and existing ordering, but does not prove attached hardware has become idle before the reset

findings.finding: Runtime suspend enters framework clock pause, but the vendor NGD transfer callback disconnects RX and TX SPS endpoints before its QMI inactive request. Returning success from framework pause therefore cannot establish idle for the modern driver; retaining endpoint handles also is not evidence of retaining a valid BAM configuration.

Modern terminate_all resets/reinitializes a queued pipe. Its own comment requires attached hardware engine activity to have stopped first. Synchronizing software callbacks and closing RX admission does not prove this hardware condition.

The current callback tears down DMA before checking the handle or sending QMI inactive. A failure leaves the framework active after DMA release; timeout additionally marks the driver asleep while returning an error. The new transaction-allocation guard prevents an invalid QMI request but deliberately leaves this state-recovery problem open.

Neither preserving DMA across collapse, merely clearing NGD CFG enable bits, nor moving QMI inactive ahead of BAM cleanup has a verified quiescence/power-access contract in these reviewed sources. No sequence is implemented solely from register names or a synthetic model.

qmi_txn_init initializes a transaction but may fail to allocate an ID. It stores the negative errno into the u16 ID. Sending or cancelling despite this failure can use the wrong ID and retire an unrelated transaction. A two-line standalone negative-error guard is independently host-qualified.

findings.area: SPS low-level trace corrects reset terminology
findings.finding: sps_disconnect -> resource-manager disconnect -> sps_bam_pipe_disconnect -> bam_pipe_exit. Despite the wrapper comments using reset, bam_pipe_exit masks pipe/EE interrupts and clears P_EN; it does not assert a reset bit or poll NGD idle. The SLIMbus RX/TX options omit SPS_O_NO_DISABLE, so this disable path is taken. It is not equivalent to modern bam_chan_init_hw pipe reset/reinitialization and does not provide the needed connected-engine stop proof.

required_before_stop_reordering: A documented NGD producer-stop sequence and acknowledgment or idle predicate, including inflight RX/TX behavior
Proof of BAM register accessibility and safe reset/release ordering across QMI inactive success and ambiguous timeout
A rollback design distinguishing allocation/send/remote refusal/timeout, preserving framework and transport state and retry ownership
Composition with lifecycle mutex, PM-independent master work, independent slave notification, parent/child/QMI gates and SSR/PM barriers

registered_endpoint_recovery_audit.finding: Discovery changes svc_info and requeues startup, but enable skips qmi_init for registered controllers; the previously connected client is retained. Full recovery must synchronize PM and active transactions/client lifetime and hardware DMA teardown, rather than silently accepting the newly advertised endpoint or merely adding a rejection guard.

decision: Keep hardware-stop and registered endpoint reconnection open. Restore original already-running-DSP bootstrap independently through existing parent/child/QMI/last-DOWN gates; this exercises the established startup path and does not invent a new stop sequence.
